sources.entry: ParrotFlow - Scriptable local dictation that uses the text on your screen to fix names, and your rules to format numbers, dates, and links.

summary.one_liner: ParrotFlow is a local, scriptable dictation app for macOS that fixes recognized text with your own rules, scripts, and optional prompts.
summary.what_it_does: ParrotFlow is a local dictation app for macOS, configured through a YAML file (config.yaml). Its pipeline runs steps on the transcribed text, such as built-in number, date, money, filler and disfluency handling, and user-defined transforms. A transform can be a regex replacement, a Python or shell script that reads stdin, or a prompt sent to a language model. The README's examples include turning PR numbers into GitHub links, adding Slack mentions, and converting spoken prices into digits. A context feature reads the on-screen text of the window being dictated into so names and identifiers like "CaretAnchor" are spelled correctly, with an exclusion list for password managers and similar apps. A vocabulary feature learns corrections the user accepts from the pill overlay. Transforms can also be triggered on demand by a button on the pill, a key press, or a spoken phrase. Language models are optional: built-in steps do not need one, and prompt steps can use a local model through Ollama or a remote API such as OpenAI. The README also describes a ParrotFlow skill for coding agents that writes and checks config rules.
use_cases: dictate code and identifiers into a terminal or editor
turn spoken numbers, prices and dates into digits
auto-link GitHub PR numbers while dictating
add Slack mentions to dictated messages
fix recurring misheard names or jargon
clean up filler words and false starts in dictation
run a grammar fix on dictated text with a local model
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh (the README's install script URL is missing; use Homebrew if unsure)
npx skills add znat/parrotflow --skill parrotflow (optional, for coding agents)
stack: Parakeet (speech recognition, named in keywords context)
notable: Custom transforms written as regex replacements, scripts, or prompts, wired into a configurable pipeline
Reads the on-screen text of the dictated window to correct names and terms, with app exclusions
Learns vocabulary corrections from accepted suggestions on the pill overlay
Built-in steps keep the user's wording and do not need a cloud key
Includes a skill for coding agents to write and validate config rules
caveats: Requires Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later
Uses about 2 GB of disk and 1 GB of memory
Context reading needs the Accessibility permission
The install script's URL is missing from the README text
Prompt transforms that rewrite text depend on a chosen model, local or cloud
